subject: math
title: Adding and Subtracting to 10 000
seo_title: Grade 4 Adding and Subtracting to 10 000 Worksheets: Regrouping and Mental Math (BC)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on adding and subtracting to 10 000, matched to the BC curriculum: mental math, column addition and subtraction with regrouping, subtracting across zeros, estimating, checking with the inverse and BC word problems. 100 questions with an answer key. Good FSA practice.
key_big: Line up the ones. Regroup when you need to. Check with the inverse.
key_sub: Try mental math first: compensate (1999 is 2000 − 1), split or count on. In columns, start on the right; every 0 you regroup across becomes 9. Estimate before you start, and add back what you took away to check.
body_html:
The idea: use place value

Numbers to 10 000 are made of thousands, hundreds, tens and ones. Add or subtract the same places. When a place gets 10 or more, regroup: 10 ones make 1 ten, 10 tens make 1 hundred, and 10 hundreds make 1 thousand.

First ask: can I do this in my head? If not, use the column method.

Mental math

Split: break both numbers into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones. Add each place, then put the parts back together.

Compensate

What is 3546 + 1999?

1999 is 1 less than 2000. Add 2000: 3546 + 2000 = 5546. You added 1 too many, so take 1 away: 5545.

Answer: 5545

Count on: when two numbers are close, count up from the smaller one to find the difference.

Column addition

Put ones under ones, tens under tens, and so on. Start on the right. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup 1 into the next column.

Column subtraction, including across zeros

Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. If the top digit is smaller, regroup 1 from the next column. If the next column is 0, go left to the first digit that is not 0. Every 0 you pass becomes 9.

Estimate, then check with the inverse

Before you start, estimate: round each number and work it out in your head. For 4678 + 2856, 5000 + 3000 = 8000, so the answer should be close to 8000.

When you finish, check with the inverse. Addition and subtraction undo each other. To check 5000 − 1268 = 3732, add: 3732 + 1268 = 5000. You get back to the start, so the answer is right.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not regrouping (4678 + 2856 = 6424)Write the regrouped 1 under the next column and add it in
Taking the smaller digit from the larger one (6152 − 2879 = 4727)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Regroup when the top is smaller
Making each 0 into 10 instead of 9 (5000 − 1268 = 3842)Only the last place gets 10. Each 0 you pass gives 1 away, so it becomes 9
Lining up the numbers on the left (4567 + 382 = 8387)Line up the ones on the right: 4567 + 382 = 4949

faq.q: What does Grade 4 learn about adding and subtracting in the BC math curriculum?
faq.a: Under Computational fluency, Grade 4 students add and subtract whole numbers to 10 000. They use mental strategies, the column method with regrouping, estimation and the inverse to check their answers.
Round one number to a friendly number, work it out, then fix the difference. For 3546 + 1999, add 2000 to get 5546, then take away 1 to get 5545.

faq.q: How do you subtract across zeros, like 5000 − 1268?
faq.a: Go left to the first digit that is not 0 and regroup from there; each 0 you pass becomes 9. 5000 becomes 4 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones, so 5000 − 1268 = 3732.

faq.q: Does adding and subtracting help with the Grade 4 FSA?
faq.a: Yes. The FSA numeracy section asks students to solve number problems, and many of them need adding or subtracting. Estimating first and checking with the inverse helps students catch mistakes.

sets.title: Estimate, then check with the inverse

items.q: Round each number to the nearest thousand to estimate 3874 + 2156.
items.e: 3874 rounds up to 4000. 2156 rounds down to 2000. 4000 + 2000 = 6000. (The exact answer is 6030, which is close.)

items.q: Round each number to the nearest thousand to estimate 7215 − 2689.
items.e: 7215 rounds down to 7000. 2689 rounds up to 3000. 7000 − 3000 = 4000. (5000 comes from cutting 2689 down to 2000 instead of rounding it.)

items.q: Round each number to the nearest hundred to estimate 2468 + 1347.
items.e: 2468 rounds up to 2500. 1347 rounds down to 1300. 2500 + 1300 = 3800. (3700 comes from cutting 2468 down to 2400 instead of rounding it.)

items.q: Round each number to the nearest hundred to estimate 6352 − 2738.
Which is the best estimate for 4985 + 2996?
items.e: 4985 is very close to 5000 and 2996 is very close to 3000. 5000 + 3000 = 8000. The exact answer is 7981.

items.q: Sofia worked out 3765 + 2847 = 5502. Estimate to the nearest thousand. Is her answer reasonable?
items.e: 3765 rounds to 4000 and 2847 rounds to 3000. 4000 + 3000 = 7000. 5502 is far from 7000, so the answer is not reasonable. (Sofia forgot to regroup. The exact answer is 6612.)

items.q: Leah worked out 8203 − 3596 = 4607. Estimate to the nearest hundred. Is her answer reasonable?
items.e: 8203 rounds to 8200 and 3596 rounds to 3600. 8200 − 3600 = 4600. 4607 is very close to 4600, so the answer is reasonable.

Which calculation checks 7241 − 3586 = 3655?
items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. Add the answer to the number you took away: 3655 + 3586 = 7241. You get back to the start, so the answer is right.

items.q: Which calculation checks 8004 − 3657 = 4347?
items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. Add the answer to the number you took away: 4347 + 3657 = 8004. You get back to the start, so the answer is right.

items.q: Which calculation checks 3687 + 2456 = 6143?
items.e: Subtraction is the inverse of addition. Take one number away from the answer: 6143 − 2456 = 3687. You get the other number, so the answer is right.

items.q: 8436 − 2758 = 5678. Which number sentence is also true?
items.e: The three numbers make a fact family. The two smaller numbers add to make the biggest: 5678 + 2758 = 8436.

sets.title: Word problems: salmon, road trips and fundraisers

items.q: Volunteers counted salmon at a viewing spot on the Adams River. They counted 3486 sockeye on Monday and 4257 on Tuesday. How many sockeye did they count on the two days?
items.e: Put the two days together, so add. 3486 + 4257 = 7743. Check: 7743 − 4257 = 3486.

items.q: The Chen family drove 2468 km in July, including a trip to Kelowna. They drove 1795 km in August. How far did they drive in the two months?
items.e: Put the two months together, so add. 2468 + 1795 = 4263. Check: 4263 − 1795 = 2468.

items.q: Our school’s Terry Fox Run raised $2385. The spring fun fair raised $1947. How much did the two events raise altogether?
On the Adams River, 6215 sockeye were counted on Saturday and 3878 on Friday. How many more were counted on Saturday?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 6215 − 3878 = 2337. Check: 2337 + 3878 = 6215.

items.q: Volunteers hope to count 10 000 salmon at the river this week. So far they have counted 7468. How many more salmon do they hope to count?
items.e: Find what is still to come, so subtract. 10 000 − 7468 = 2532. Check: 2532 + 7468 = 10 000.

items.q: The Martin family planned a 2000 km summer road trip to Kelowna and around the Okanagan. They have driven 1385 km. How many kilometres are left?
items.e: Find the distance left, so subtract. 2000 − 1385 = 615. Check: 615 + 1385 = 2000.

items.q: Grouse Mountain had 4206 visitors on Saturday and 2758 visitors on Sunday. How many more visitors came on Saturday?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 4206 − 2758 = 1448. Check: 1448 + 2758 = 4206.

items.q: Volunteers counted some salmon in the morning. They counted 2375 more in the afternoon. The total for the day was 6012. How many salmon did they count in the morning?
items.e: Work backwards. Take away the 2375 that were added: 6012 − 2375 = 3637. Check: 3637 + 2375 = 6012.

items.q: On Friday, 2648 salmon were counted at the river. On Saturday, 1875 more were counted than on Friday. How many salmon were counted on the two days?
items.e: Step 1, Saturday’s count: 2648 + 1875 = 4523. Step 2, both together: 2648 + 4523 = 7171.

items.q: A hatchery on Vancouver Island raised 8000 coho salmon fry. It let 3465 go in one creek and 2780 in another creek. How many fry are still at the hatchery?
items.e: Step 1, fry let go: 3465 + 2780 = 6245. Step 2, fry still at the hatchery: 8000 − 6245 = 1755.

items.q: A tour bus drove 3264 km on trips to Kelowna in June. In July it drove 875 km less. How far did it drive in the two months?
A truck driver plans to drive 5000 km this month, taking fruit from Kelowna. She drove 1648 km in week 1 and 1875 km in week 2. How many kilometres are left?
items.e: Step 1, kilometres driven: 1648 + 1875 = 3523. Step 2, kilometres left: 5000 − 3523 = 1477.

items.q: Ava’s family drove 1386 km to Kelowna and back, then 958 km on day trips. Owen’s family drove 3000 km on their holiday. How many more kilometres did Owen’s family drive?
items.e: Step 1, Ava’s family: 1386 + 958 = 2344. Step 2, find the difference: 3000 − 2344 = 656.

items.q: The school wants to raise $10 000 for new library books. The fall fun fair raised $3846 and the read-a-thon raised $2675. How much more does the school need?
items.e: Step 1, money raised: $3846 + $2675 = $6521. Step 2, money still needed: $10 000 − $6521 = $3479.

items.q: The school had $6325 in its field trip fund. It spent $2958 on buses to Science World. Then a bottle drive raised $1475. How much money is in the fund now?
items.e: Step 1, after spending: $6325 − $2958 = $3367. Step 2, after the bottle drive: $3367 + $1475 = $4842.

items.q: Chloe’s class raised $1475 at a bottle drive. Simran’s class raised $386 more. How much did the two classes raise altogether?
items.e: Step 1, Simran’s class: $1475 + $386 = $1861. Step 2, both together: $1475 + $1861 = $3336.

items.q: A BC Ferries boat carried 3486 passengers in the morning and 2875 passengers in the afternoon. How many passengers did it carry that day?
items.e: Put the two parts of the day together, so add. 3486 + 2875 = 6361. Check: 6361 − 2875 = 3486.

items.q: The Terry Fox Run had 5000 bottles of water. Runners took 2486 bottles in the morning and 1397 at lunch. How many bottles were left?
items.e: Step 1, bottles taken: 2486 + 1397 = 3883. Step 2, bottles left: 5000 − 3883 = 1117.

items.q: A food bank in Surrey had 4062 cans of food. It gave out 2785 cans. Then a school food drive brought in 1938 cans. How many cans does the food bank have now?
items.e: Step 1, after giving out: 4062 − 2785 = 1277. Step 2, after the food drive: 1277 + 1938 = 3215.
